instruction: Use Abaqus/CAE through the graphical user interface to perform a steady-state heat conduction analysis. Use SI units (meters) or convert material properties appropriately for the chosen unit system. Model Definition: Create a 3D Deformable Solid part using Extrusion. Sketch a rectangle from (0, 0) to (100, 50) in the X-Y plane and extrude along the global Z-axis to a thickness of 10 mm. This produces a plate with in-plane dimensions 100 mm x 50 mm and thickness 10 mm. Material and Section: Define a material named Copper with thermal conductivity = 400 W/(m·K). Note that SI units (meters) should be used, or the conductivity should be converted to 0.0004 W/(mm·K) if using millimeters. Create a Solid Homogeneous section using Copper and assign it to the entire plate. Assembly: Create one dependent instance of the plate. Analysis Step: Create a Heat Transfer, Steady-state step named Step-Thermal. Loads and Boundary Conditions: Apply a temperature of 100 degC to the end face at X = 0 (the face with normal in -X, dimensions 50 mm x 10 mm). Apply a temperature of 20 degC to the end face at X = 100 mm (the face with normal in +X, dimensions 50 mm x 10 mm). Keep all other faces adiabatic by applying no thermal boundary condition to them. Discretization: Mesh the plate with a global seed size of 5 mm. Assign the element type DC3D8 and generate the mesh. Job Execution: Create a job named Job-Thermal, submit it for analysis, and wait for the analysis to complete successfully. Deliverables: Save the model database as C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\Job-Thermal.cae and ensure the output database is generated as C:\Users\Administrator\Desktop\Job-Thermal.odb.
